mainTopic: Pauses in שופר, the link between the blasts and the ברכות of ראש השנה, and whether the שליח ציבור prays on everyone's behalf
overview: This amud begins with רבי יוחנן's ruling that the nine שופר blasts may be heard at nine different times of the day, and a ברייתא supports it. The גמרא tests this against רבי יוחנן's strict rulings about pausing in הלל, מגילה and קריאת שמע. It concludes that those strict rulings were either his teacher's view or said according to the questioner's view. Next, a ברייתא teaches that on ראש השנה the blasts and the ברכות all depend on each other. רבה explains why: מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות are one package, carried out through the שופר. The גמרא then shows that the blasts ideally follow the order of the ברכות, but רבא and a ברייתא limit this to a חבר עיר. The ברייתא adds that one person may blow for another but may not say the ברכות for him. It also teaches that שופר takes priority over the ברכות, even when the שופר is only a possibility. Finally, the גמרא turns to the dispute between רבן גמליאל and the חכמים over whether the שליח ציבור fulfills everyone's obligation. The אמוראים disagree about whether the חכמים conceded, and a challenge to רבי יוחנן's report continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Nine blasts at nine different times still count
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that hearing the nine שופר blasts spread across nine different times of the day fulfills the obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If one heard] nine שופר blasts at nine different times of the day, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of a ruling by רבי יוחנן, which started at the end of the previous page. He says the nine blasts do not need to be heard one right after the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nine blasts are the three sets of תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה. רבי יוחנן holds that long gaps between them do not ruin the מצוה. This lenient position about pauses is what the rest of this passage will test.

keyTerms.meaning: שופר blasts. Here it means all nine required sounds.
Times or hours. Here it means separate points spread across the day.
He has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in mid-sentence. The opening words, 'אמר רבי יוחנן: שמע' (רבי יוחנן said: one who heard), are at the end of the previous page. That is why the challenge in step 3 is aimed at רבי יוחנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling becomes the anchor of the whole passage. The next steps support it and then test whether it fits with other rulings by רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: [If one heard] nine blasts at nine times of the day —
phrases.notes: Continues 'רבי יוחנן said: one who heard' from the previous page.

phrases.english: he has fulfilled [his obligation].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling by רבי יוחנן that began on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The nine שופר blasts do not need to be heard in a row. Hearing them at nine separate times of the day is enough.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the ruling and adds details
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule as רבי יוחנן. It adds that hearing nine people blow at once does not work, but hearing different blasts from different people does work, even with gaps and across the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: If one heard nine blasts at nine times of the day, he has fulfilled his obligation. If he heard them from nine people all at once, he has not fulfilled it. If he heard a תקיעה from this person and a תרועה from that person, he has fulfilled it. This is true even with gaps in between, and even if it took the entire day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי יוחנן said, which backs up his ruling. The ברייתא also adds a few related cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats the case of nine blasts at nine times, which confirms רבי יוחנן. It then adds one case that fails: nine people blowing at once. In that case the blasts are not heard in their proper order, one after another. It also adds a case that works: different blowers, as long as the order is kept, even with breaks across the whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also taught this way.' This formula introduces a ברייתא that supports what was just said.
At once, at the same time.
The broken, wavering שופר sound.
With gaps or interruptions, not continuous.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'nine' cases. Nine blasts at nine different times works. Nine people blowing at the same moment does not work. Spreading the blasts out over time is fine. Hearing them all overlapping, with no order, is the problem.

phrases.english: This is also taught [in a ברייתא]:
If one heard nine blasts
at nine times of the day — he has fulfilled [his obligation].
[If he heard them] from nine people at once —
he has not fulfilled [his obligation].
A תקיעה from this one and a תרועה from that one —
he has fulfilled [his obligation].
And even with interruptions,
and even [spread over] the entire day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the nine blasts may be spread out over the day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that states the same rule and adds related cases: blowers at the same time fail, different blowers in order succeed, and gaps are fine.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוחנן's ruling about הלל and מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן can allow long gaps for שופר. He himself said that for הלל and מגילה, a pause long enough to finish the whole thing forces you to start again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: for הלל and for the מגילה, if one paused long enough to finish all of it, he goes back to the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן with another statement he made. That statement seems to say the opposite about long pauses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שופר, רבי יוחנן said a long gap is fine. For הלל and מגילה, he said a long gap means you must restart. Both cases involve one מצוה made up of parts, so his two rulings look like they contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Did he really say...?' This opens a challenge.
'But didn't he say...?' This brings in a conflicting statement.
He paused or waited.
Long enough to complete the whole thing.
He goes back to the beginning.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yoḥanan say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
With hallel and with the Megilla,

phrases.aramaic: אִם שָׁהָה כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ —
phrases.english: if he paused long enough to complete all of it —
he goes back to the beginning!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ruling has been supported, the גמרא tests whether it fits with other statements by רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's lenient ruling in step 1 that long gaps between שופר blasts are fine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן also stated that a long pause in הלל or מגילה forces a restart. This seems to contradict his leniency about pauses for שופר.

steps.title: One ruling is his own, the other is his teacher's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the lenient שופר ruling is רבי יוחנן's own view. The strict הלל and מגילה ruling is his teacher רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק's view, which he was only quoting.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one is his own view, and that one is his teacher's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. It says the two rulings come from two different people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the הלל and מגילה ruling 'in the name of' his teacher, so he was reporting someone else's opinion. His own personal opinion is the lenient one about pauses. With two different authors, there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult.' This opens an answer.
This one is his own view.
That one is his teacher's view.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not reverse them. 'דידיה' (his own) is the lenient שופר ruling. 'דרביה' (his teacher's) is the strict ruling about restarting הלל and מגילה.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is his own [view], that is his teacher's [view].

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דִידֵיהּ, הָא דְרַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different speakers: the two rulings are assigned to two different authorities.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings reflect רבי יוחנן's own view, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן personally holds that long pauses are fine. The strict restart rule belongs to his teacher, רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק.

steps.title: Story: רבי יוחנן told רבי אבהו to restart שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. A story shows רבי יוחנן personally ruling that a long pause in קריאת שמע requires starting over.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it not his own view? But רבי אבהו was once walking behind רבי יוחנן and reciting קריאת שמע. When he reached filthy alleyways, he fell silent. After he passed through, he said to him: What about finishing [from where I stopped]? He answered him: If you paused long enough to complete all of it, go back to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer from step 4. It brings a story where רבי יוחנן himself, not just quoting his teacher, told someone to restart after a long pause. The answer to this challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the strict 'restart' rule was only the teacher's view. In this story, though, רבי יוחנן gives the strict ruling in his own name, as practical advice to his student. So it seems the strict view is his own after all, and the contradiction with the שופר ruling returns.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And is it not his own [view]?' This opens a challenge to the previous answer.
Was walking along.
Filthy alleyways, where it is forbidden to say holy words.
He fell silent.
What is the law about finishing [from where I stopped]?

phrases.english: And is it not his own [view]?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל וְאָזֵיל
phrases.english: But Rabbi Abbahu was walking along
behind Rabbi Yoḥanan
and was reciting Shema,
when he reached filthy alleyways,
he fell silent,
after he passed through,
he said to him: What about completing [it]?
He said to him: If you paused
long enough to complete all of it —
go back to the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִידֵיהּ לָא? וְהָא רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה שָׁקֵיל וְאָזֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from step 4 by showing that the strict view was also רבי יוחנן's own personal ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 4 that the strict 'restart after a long pause' rule is only the teacher's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן personally told רבי אבהו to restart קריאת שמע after a long pause. So the strict view is his own, and it again clashes with his lenient שופר ruling.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן Was Answering by the Other Person's View
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן's strict ruling about קריאת שמע was not his own opinion. He was answering the questioner according to the questioner's own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי יוחנן meant: 'I myself do not hold that a pause is a problem. But you do hold that it is a problem. So by your view, if you paused long enough to finish the whole thing, go back to the beginning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the earlier answer from step 4. It shows that the קריאת שמע story does not prove what רבי יוחנן personally held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 5 assumed that רבי יוחנן's ruling in the story was his own opinion. The גמרא says he was only answering by the other person's view. His own view, that a pause does not break a מצוה, still stands. So there is no contradiction with his lenient שופר ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant to tell him (a reinterpretation)
According to me / in my own view
According to you / in your view
Go back to the beginning

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוחנן changed his mind. He gave a ruling that fit the questioner's view, not his own.

phrases.english: This is what he said to him:
I myself do not hold this,
but for you, since you do hold it:

phrases.aramaic: אִם שָׁהִיתָ כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ —
phrases.english: if you paused long enough to finish all of it
go back to the beginning.
phrases.notes: Refers to קריאת שמע from the story in step 5.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and saves the answer of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the ruling was given according to the other person's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן personally held that a long pause in קריאת שמע requires starting over.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was only answering by the questioner's view. He himself holds that a pause does not break a מצוה, which fits his שופר ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's own view is that pauses do not break a מצוה. The strict rulings were either quoted from his teacher or said according to someone else's view.

steps.title: Which Blasts and Blessings Are Required
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the general rule: missing some תקיעות or ברכות does not ruin the rest. But on ראש השנה and on יום הכפורים of the יובל, all of them are required.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The blasts do not hold each other back. The blessings do not hold each other back. But the blasts and blessings of ראש השנה and of יום הכפורים do hold each other back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ברייתא. The ברייתא states when all the blasts and blessings are required together, and when each one counts on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not holding each other back' means that if you can only do some of them, the ones you do still count. On ראש השנה, and on יום הכפורים of the יובל year (when a שופר is blown), the set is all-or-nothing. Sefaria explains the first two clauses as the blasts and added blessings of a fast day (תענית).

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
They hold each other back; each one is required for the others to count
Shofar or trumpet blasts
The special added blessings in the תפילה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: תְּקִיעוֹת — אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ.
phrases.english: Blasts do not hold each other back.

phrases.aramaic: בְּרָכוֹת — אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ.
phrases.english: Blessings do not hold each other back.
The blasts and blessings of Rosh HaShana
and of Yom Kippur do hold each other back.
phrases.notes: יום הכפורים of the יובל year, when the שופר is blown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the pause discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש השנה and on יום הכפורים, all the blasts and blessings are required. Elsewhere, each one counts on its own.

steps.title: Why Are They All Required on ראש השנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that ראש השנה's blasts and blessings are all-or-nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא wants the reason behind the ברייתא's rule, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a rule but no reason. The גמרא wants to know what makes ראש השנה different from other days.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ראש השנה blasts and blessings hold each other back.

steps.title: רבה: מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות Are One Package
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that הקדוש ברוך הוא asked for מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות together as one unit. So you cannot do just part of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: הקדוש ברוך הוא said, 'Say before Me on ראש השנה מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות. מלכיות, so you will make Me King over you. זכרונות, so your remembrance will come before Me for good. And with what? With the שופר.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. All three sections work together as one request from ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crowning ה׳ and being remembered for good are carried out 'with the שופר.' This makes all three parts one connected unit. Since it is one unit, missing any part means the whole מצוה was not done.

keyTerms.meaning: Kingship verses: accepting ה׳ as King
Remembrance verses: asking to be remembered for good
Shofar verses
That you will crown Me as King
And with what? With the שופר

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the idea that the three central ברכות of ראש השנה מוסף are one connected service.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Say before Me on Rosh HaShana
Kingship, Remembrances and Shofarot.
Kingship, so that you will crown Me King over you;
Remembrances, so that there will come before Me
your remembrance for good.
And with what? With the shofar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three sections are one request from ה׳, carried out together through the שופר, so they hold each other back.
steps.whatToRemember: On ראש השנה, מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות are one package, and each part is needed.

steps.title: משנה: Got a שופר Only After Davening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. Someone who said the ברכות and only afterward got a שופר blows the sets of תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who said the blessings, and only afterward a שופר became available to him, blows תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from the משנה in order to analyze it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the blasts are done separately from the ברכות, all together after davening. The case is simple: he had no שופר during davening. This sets up the inference in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It became available to him
He blows a תקיעה, a תרועה and a תקיעה

phrases.english: One who recited the blessings
and afterward a shofar became available to him,
blows a tekia, a terua and a tekia.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁבֵּירַךְ וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְמַנָּה לוֹ שׁוֹפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה, still about blasts and blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the שופר came only after the ברכות, he blows the sets afterward.

steps.title: Inference: Normally Blow During the Blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה's wording that this is allowed only because he had no שופר at first. If he had one from the start, he must hear the blasts in the order of the ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that he did not have a שופר at the start. But if he had a שופר at the start, when he hears the blasts, he must hear them in the order of the blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and pulls out a hidden rule. Normally the blasts belong inside the ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stresses that the שופר came 'afterward.' This shows that blowing everything at the end is only a fallback. When a שופר is available, the right way is to blow a set after each special ברכה (מלכיות, זכרונות, שופרות). This fits רבה's idea that the blessings and the שופר go together.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is only because (signals an inference from wording)
From the start
But this implies that
In the order of the blessings

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say that the blasts after davening are useless. It says that blowing after davening is the fallback, used only when there was no שופר earlier.

phrases.aramaic: טַעְמָא דְּלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ שׁוֹפָר מֵעִיקָּרָא,
phrases.english: The reason is that he did not have a shofar at the start;
but if he had a shofar at the start,
when he hears them,
he must hear them by the order of the blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ שׁוֹפָר מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When a שופר is available, the blasts should be heard in the order of the ברכות, one set after each special blessing.
steps.whatToRemember: The ideal is to blow the שופר inside the ברכות. Blowing all of it afterward is only a fallback for when there was no שופר at first.

steps.title: רב פפא בר שמואל asks his attendant to blow after each blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל prays alone and tells his attendant to blow the שופר whenever he signals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא בר שמואל stood up to pray. He told his attendant: 'When I signal to you, blow the שופר for me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real practice. It is setting up רבא's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 taught that when a שופר is available, the blasts should be heard in the order of the ברכות. רב פפא בר שמואל applied this to his own private prayer. He planned to signal after each section so the blasts would fall in the right places.

keyTerms.meaning: to pray (here, the מוסף prayer of ראש השנה)
his attendant (the student who served him)
when I signal to you
blow (the שופר)

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל קָם לְצַלּוֹיֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel stood up to pray,
he said to his attendant:
When I signal to you, blow for me.
phrases.notes: He wanted the blasts placed after each of the blessing sections.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל קָם לְצַלּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the conclusion of step 11 (hear the blasts in the order of the ברכות) to an individual praying alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא בר שמואל acted as if an individual praying alone must also hear the blasts in the order of the ברכות.

steps.title: רבא: the order of the blessings matters only in a community setting
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב פפא בר שמואל that the rule of blowing in the order of the ברכות was said only for a חבר עיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: 'They only said this rule for a חבר עיר (a community praying together).'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רב פפא בר שמואל's practice. He limits the rule from step 11 to a community setting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that the blasts must line up with the ברכות is real, but it applies only when there is a חבר עיר, a congregation praying together. A person praying alone does not need to stop and blow after each section.

keyTerms.meaning: they only said (this rule) in the case of…
a community prayer group / a quorum of ten

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the order of the ברכות never matters. It still matters with a חבר עיר. He is only saying that an individual is not bound by it.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
They said this only in the case of a ḥever ir (a community quorum).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the practice in step 12 by narrowing the scope of the rule in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying the 'order of the ברכות' rule to an individual praying alone.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rule was given only for a חבר עיר, not for a יחיד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearing the blasts in the order of the ברכות is required only in a חבר עיר.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the order of the ברכות matters only in a חבר עיר. Without one, the blasts must still be in their proper sets but need not follow the ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא: When a person hears the blasts, he hears them in order, and according to the order of the ברכות. When is this said? With a חבר עיר. But without a חבר עיר, he hears them in order, but not according to the order of the ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבא said, as support for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא separates two kinds of order. 'In order' means each set must be תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה, and this always applies. The 'order of the ברכות' means blowing after each blessing section, and this applies only in a חבר עיר.

keyTerms.meaning: it is also taught this way (in a ברייתא), as support
in order: the proper sequence of each set (תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה)
the order of the blessings: blowing after each blessing section
in what case is this said?

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'orders' here. The order of the blasts within a set always matters. Only the matching with the ברכות depends on having a חבר עיר.

phrases.english: It is also taught so (in a baraita):
When he hears them, he hears them in order,
and according to the order of the blessings.
In what case is this said? With a ḥever ir.
But where there is no ḥever ir,
he hears them in order,
but not according to the order of the blessings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's limitation in step 13 with a תנאי source.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that the order of the ברכות applies only in a חבר עיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says the same distinction explicitly.
steps.whatToRemember: The sets of blasts must always be in proper order. Blowing after each ברכה is required only in a חבר עיר.

steps.title: One may blow for another, but not say the blessings for another
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a friend may blow שופר for someone who did not blow, but may not say the ברכות on behalf of someone who did not say them.
steps.simpleTranslation: An individual who did not blow: his friend may blow for him. An individual who did not say the ברכות: his friend may not say them on his behalf.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא adds a new rule. It compares doing the שופר for someone else with saying the ברכות for someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of שופר is hearing the blast, so another person's blowing works for the listener. The ברכות are תפילה, a personal request to הקדוש ברוך הוא. Each individual must say them himself, so another individual cannot say them for him.

keyTerms.meaning: an individual (not a community)
his friend / another person
says the blessings on his behalf

phrases.aramaic: וְיָחִיד שֶׁלֹּא תָּקַע — חֲבֵירוֹ תּוֹקֵעַ לוֹ,
phrases.english: And an individual who did not blow, his friend blows for him;

phrases.aramaic: וְיָחִיד שֶׁלֹּא בֵּירַךְ — אֵין חֲבֵירוֹ מְבָרֵךְ עָלָיו.
phrases.english: but an individual who did not say the blessings, his friend does not say the blessings for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיָחִיד שֶׁלֹּא תָּקַע חֲבֵירוֹ תּוֹקֵעַ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new rule about doing the מצוה for someone else.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blowing שופר can be done by one individual for another; saying the ברכות cannot.

steps.title: Shofar takes priority over the blessings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that שופר is the bigger מצוה. If one must choose between a town with blowing and a town with ברכות, he goes to the town with blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מצוה with those who blow is greater than with those who say the ברכות. How so? There are two towns. In one they blow, and in the other they say the ברכות. One goes to the place where they blow, and does not go to the place where they say the ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a rule of priority between שופר and the ברכות, and explains it with a case of two towns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person cannot have both, the שופר wins. He travels to the town where someone can blow, even though that means missing the ברכות said in the other town.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה is greater with those who blow
how so? (introduces an example)
towns

phrases.english: And the מצוה with those who blow is greater than with those who say the blessings.
How so?
Two towns:
in one they blow, and in the other they say the blessings,
one goes to the place where they blow,
and does not go to the place where they say the blessings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a priority rule between שופר and the ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one cannot have both, hearing שופר takes priority over the ברכות.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to teach this. שופר is from the Torah and the ברכות are rabbinic, so of course שופר comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! This one (שופר) is דאורייתא, and that one (the ברכות) is דרבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's priority rule. It argues the rule is so obvious that there is no reason to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Torah מצוה naturally outranks a rabbinic one. So the ruling that one should choose שופר over the ברכות seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious! (why does this need to be said?)
from the Torah
from the Rabbis

phrases.english: It is obvious!
This one is from the Torah, and that one is rabbinic!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's priority of שופר over the ברכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah law clearly outranks a rabbinic law, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Needed even when the שופר is uncertain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ruling teaches something new. Even when the ברכות are certain and the שופר is only a doubt, one still goes to the town with the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed. It teaches that even though this one (the ברכות) is certain and that one (the שופר) is only a doubt, one still goes for the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by showing a case where the ruling is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a sure rabbinic מצוה is better than a Torah מצוה that might not happen. The ברייתא teaches that even then, the possible Torah מצוה of שופר takes priority.

keyTerms.meaning: no, it is needed (for a less obvious case)
certain
doubtful / uncertain

steps.whatToRemember: שופר beats the ברכות even when the ברכות are certain and the שופר is only a possibility.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a general priority principle: a possible Torah מצוה can outweigh a certain rabbinic one.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּהָא וַדַּאי וְהָא סָפֵק.
phrases.english: for even though this one is certain and that one is doubtful.
phrases.notes: The ברכות are certain to happen; whether the שופר will be blown is uncertain.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּהָא וַדַּאי וְהָא סָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: the ruling applies to a less obvious scenario (certain rabbinic vs. doubtful Torah).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A certain rabbinic מצוה might be preferred over a doubtful Torah מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a doubtful שופר takes priority over certain ברכות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Go to the town with the שופר even if the blowing there is uncertain.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: every individual must pray
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: just as the שליח ציבור must pray, every individual must pray too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the prayer leader is obligated, so too every single individual is obligated, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the משנה by quoting its opening words. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה continues with רבן גמליאל's opinion that the שליח ציבור fulfills the obligation for everyone. The וכו׳ ("etc.") points to that unquoted part, which is what the coming ברייתא is about.

keyTerms.meaning: The prayer leader who prays out loud for the congregation
An individual person
Obligated

phrases.english: Just as the prayer leader is obligated,
so too every single individual, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: רבן גמליאל says the שליח ציבור fulfills the obligation for the many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of שופר and ברכות and moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, each individual must pray for himself, just like the שליח ציבור.

steps.title: The חכמים ask רבן גמליאל why the congregation prays at all
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the חכמים challenging רבן גמליאל: if the leader prays for everyone, why does the congregation say its own silent prayer?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: They said to רבן גמליאל: According to your view, why does the congregation pray?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים attack רבן גמליאל's view by pointing to a practice everyone follows. Everyone says the quiet עמידה before the leader repeats it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שליח ציבור's prayer covers everyone, the congregation's own silent prayer seems pointless. The חכמים use this common practice to show that each person must pray for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
According to your view
They pray

phrases.english: It was taught: They said to Rabban Gamliel:
According to your words, why does the congregation pray?!
phrases.notes: This refers to the silent עמידה that everyone says before the leader's repetition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that spells out the dispute in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's view that the שליח ציבור fulfills everyone's obligation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the leader covers everyone, the congregation's silent prayer would serve no purpose.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: the silent prayer gives the leader time to prepare
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answers that the congregation prays first so that the שליח ציבור can arrange his own prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: In order that the prayer leader can arrange his prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל explains why the silent prayer exists, even according to his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silent prayer is not needed for the congregation's own obligation. Its purpose is to give the leader a quiet chance to get his prayer in order before saying it out loud for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: To arrange or prepare
His prayer

phrases.english: He said to them: In order that
the prayer leader may arrange his prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the practice a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The silent prayer exists to fulfill each person's own obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The silent prayer exists so the leader can prepare his prayer.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל asks the חכמים why the leader repeats the prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל turns the question around: if everyone prays for himself, why does the שליח ציבור repeat the prayer before the ark?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to them: According to your view, why does the prayer leader go down before the ark?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבן גמליאל challenges the חכמים with a different common practice: the leader's repetition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each person must pray for himself and has already done so, the leader's loud repetition seems unnecessary. רבן גמליאל uses this practice to argue that the leader is praying on behalf of others.

keyTerms.meaning: According to your (plural) view
Goes down before the ark, meaning he leads the prayer

steps.confusionAlert: "Goes down" does not mean he leaves the room. In the old synagogues the leader's place in front of the ark was lower than the floor, so leading the prayer was called "going down before the ark."

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to them: According to your words,

phrases.aramaic: לָמָּה שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר יוֹרֵד לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה?
phrases.english: why does the prayer leader go down before the ark?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵיכֶם, לָמָּה שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר יוֹרֵד לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 20. Now רבן גמליאל questions the חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's view that every individual must pray for himself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If everyone has already prayed for himself, the leader's repetition would serve no purpose.

steps.title: The חכמים: the repetition is for those who cannot pray themselves
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the repetition fulfills the obligation of people who do not know how to pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: To fulfill the obligation of one who is not an expert.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים defend their view by limiting who the repetition is for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In their view, the leader's prayer does help some people, but only those who cannot say the prayer on their own. Someone who knows how to pray must still pray himself.

keyTerms.meaning: To fulfill the obligation on behalf of someone else
An expert, someone who knows how to say the prayer

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כְּדֵי לְהוֹצִיא אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי.
phrases.english: They said to him: In order to fulfill the obligation of one who is not an expert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the practice to a specific group
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The repetition must be for everyone, which would prove רבן גמליאל right.
steps.terutzMaskana: The repetition is only for those who cannot pray by themselves.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: if it works for one, it works for all
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל rejects the answer: if the leader can fulfill the obligation for someone who cannot pray, he can do the same for someone who can.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Just as he fulfills the obligation of one who is not an expert, so too he fulfills the obligation of the expert.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל pushes back on the חכמים's answer and turns it into support for his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים already admitted that the leader's prayer can count for someone else. רבן גמליאל argues there is no reason this should depend on whether the listener could have prayed alone. The ability to pray yourself does not take away the leader's power to pray for you.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as
Fulfills the obligation for another person

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the last word in the ברייתא, which makes it look as if רבן גמליאל won the debate. That impression is exactly what the אמוראים argue about next.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמּוֹצִיא אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי,
phrases.english: He said to them: Just as he fulfills the obligation of one who is not an expert,
so too he fulfills the obligation of the expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמּוֹצִיא אֶת שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי, כָּךְ מוֹצִיא אֶת הַבָּקִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer the חכמים gave in Step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The חכמים's answer that the repetition is only for those who cannot pray.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Once the leader can fulfill anyone's obligation, there is no reason to exclude the expert.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the חכמים agreed with רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the חכמים ended up agreeing with רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא tells us how the debate in the ברייתא ended. According to this report, רבן גמליאל's last argument convinced the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ended with רבן גמליאל's argument and no reply from the חכמים. רבי יוחנן reads this to mean the חכמים gave in and accepted his view.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who reports statements of רבי יוחנן
They agree or concede
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The Sages concede to Rabban Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells us how the ברייתא's debate ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים accepted רבן גמליאל's view.

steps.title: רב: the dispute still stands
steps.stepSummary: רב disagrees and says the חכמים never gave in. The dispute remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: It is still a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives the opposite reading of how the debate ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that the חכמים's silence at the end of the ברייתא does not mean they agreed. Both opinions remain.

keyTerms.meaning: Still
A dispute

phrases.english: And Rav said: It is still a dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the report in Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים did not concede. They still disagree with רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: רבי חייא passes רב's view on to רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בריה דרבה בר נחמני heard this teaching and told רב דימי בר חיננא that רב said the dispute still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בריה דרבה בר נחמני heard it, went, and said the teaching before רב דימי בר חיננא. He told him: This is what רב said: It is still a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about how רב's view was passed along. This sets up רב דימי's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא reports only רב's view. That sets up the next step, where רב דימי shows that another אמורא held the same view.

keyTerms.meaning: He heard it
He went
A teaching or halachic ruling
Before him, in his presence

phrases.aramaic: שַׁמְעַהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר נַחְמָנִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya, son of Rabba bar Nachmani, heard it,
went and said the teaching
before Rav Dimi bar Chinnana.
He said to him: This is what Rav said:
It is still a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁמְעַהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells how רב's view from Step 26 was passed on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's view, that the dispute still stands, is reported to רב דימי בר חיננא.

steps.title: רב דימי: ריש לקיש also said the dispute still stands
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says רבה בר בר חנה himself reported more: when רבי יוחנן said the חכמים agreed, ריש לקיש disagreed and said the dispute still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבה בר בר חנה also said this. When רבי יוחנן said this teaching, ריש לקיש disagreed with him and said: It is still a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי adds a fuller version of רבה בר בר חנה's report. That version shows that רב is not alone in his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same reporter, רבה בר בר חנה, said that ריש לקיש rejected רבי יוחנן's statement. So רב's view, that the dispute still stands, is also held by ריש לקיש in ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Also
He disagreed with him
רבי יוחנן's main study partner, who often disagrees with him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה נָמֵי הָכִי קָאָמַר.
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabba bar bar Chana also says this.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Yochanan said this teaching,
Reish Lakish disagreed with him and said:
It is still a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה נָמֵי הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי חייא's report in Step 27 by showing that רב's view has more support.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש, like רב, holds that the חכמים still disagree with רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really say the חכמים agreed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's statement. Another report quotes him saying "the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל," and that wording implies the חכמים still disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי חנה ציפוראה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל. Saying 'הלכתא' implies that they disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two reports in the name of רבי יוחנן contradict each other. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only rule "the הלכה follows X" when there is still a live disagreement to decide. So רבי חנה ציפוראה's report implies רבי יוחנן thought the חכמים still disagreed. That contradicts the report that he said the חכמים conceded.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say? (opens a challenge)
The binding law
By implication
That they disagree

steps.confusionAlert: The two reports agree on the practical outcome: we follow רבן גמליאל. The question is only whether רבי יוחנן thought the חכמים still disagreed. The wording "הלכה" implies a disagreement still exists.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חָנָה צִיפּוֹרָאָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But Rabbi Chana of Tzippori said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The halacha follows Rabban Gamliel,
saying 'the halacha' implies that they disagree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 25 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי יוחנן said the חכמים concede to רבן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling of "the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל" only makes sense if the חכמים still disagree, which contradicts the claim that they conceded.
